Sorry to say Elon, you can’t beat those Indian oligarchs even if you’re the richest person alive. Those oligarchs give out the cheapest internet on the planet that even you can’t afford to match. India was basically getting free internet in late 2016, and from 2016 to 2026 the average cost of data crashed down to like 10 cents per gigabyte (₹7 to ₹10) or even less. Nowadays with 5G, these oligarchs are giving out near 1 Gbps speeds for pennies, and home broadband is even cheaper for like $5 to $18 (₹400 to ₹1,500) a month, you get unlimited fiber up to 3.3 TB, speeds up to 1 Gbps, and every major OTT subscription bundled in. 

Compare that to your pricing. You’re talking about charging ₹30,000+($300+) upfront just for a dish kit and around ₹8,000+ ($100) every single month. Even if you burn cash and make it free for the first year, the second you hike prices back to Western rates, Indians will completely fuck you over just like how Tesla got fucked in India against local players.

Massive respect to you, of course, because that’s the exact kind of bank balance anyone dreams of having :). Massive respect for that bank balance, and for revolutionizing payments first with email-based money transfer, then electric cars, and then private reusable rockets you’ve inspired a lot of us for literally everything, and everyday, but yeah, India is an entirely different game. Those book theories and MBA frameworks don't work in India in front of Marwari, Jain, or Gujarati maths :). Running the exact same playbook everywhere just doesn't work. If you want to come to India, you have to learn jugaad, cutthroat bargaining, trust, and how to deliver crazy volume at dirt-cheap prices.

Indians are already pulling 1 Gbps speeds for pocket change, so try building an infrastructure that cheap before thinking you can take on these oligarchs. In fact, you should pray those Indian oligarchs don't enter the US or Europe market, because if they bring those prices over there, your bank balance will get completely fucked. Until you drop Starlink down to 5 to 10 cents a gig and make the hardware basically free, nobody here is touching it.

result.text:
I just unboxed Tesla’s Model Y Dual Zone Fridge and installed it in my Cybertruck. Yes, Tesla designed it for the Model Y, but I’m putting it in the truck anyway bc I spend a lot of time on the road, and I want cold drinks and fresh food with me without constantly buying ice or digging through a cooler full of water.

It’s $595 and weighs 32.6 pounds. For anyone checking whether it’ll fit their setup, it measures 26.6 inches long, 16.9 inches wide, and 14.2 inches tall. In a Model Y, it’s designed to sit in the sub-trunk and plug into the trunk outlet. Tesla says it’s compatible with every Model Y. 

The two separate temperature zones are what makes this fridge awesome. You can adjust the range from 0°F to 68°F for each side, so you can keep drinks and food refrigerated on one side while using the other as a freezer. I love having that choice instead of everything sitting at the same temperature. The center divider also comes out when you need just one larger compartment, and putting it back simply restores the two-zone setup.

Getting it powered in the Cybertruck takes an extra step bc the truck’s bed outlets supply 120-volt and 240-volt AC power, not the connection this fridge uses. So for my setup, I used a 120-volt AC-to-12-volt DC converter rated at 15 amps and 180 watts. That plugs into one of the regular 120-volt bed outlets, and the fridge’s supplied cord plugs into the converter.

Now I’ve got Starlink hooked up to the back of my Cybertruck and a fridge and freezer to go with it. I can get work done, grab a cold drink, and keep fresh food with me wherever I go. At this point, I’m pretty sure I could actually live in this thing. 

The Tesla fridge is so freakin awesome!

You can grab the fridge here too: https://t.co/VO450fQmKF
